learning_outcomes.text: Acquire basic general knowledge about computer systems.
Know and use the various numbering systems used in computer systems.
Know and use various information encoding methods used in computer systems.
Acquire the ability to use their own language in understanding computer systems, both orally and in writing, being rigorous in explanations of any process.
Acquire good handling of the recommended bibliography in the subject, so that self-sufficiency is promoted when completing training.
Know how to use the Windows operating system at a user level.
Become familiar with the use of the Internet: email, information searches, messaging services, etc.
Acquire generic knowledge about programming languages.
Learn to use the spreadsheet as a programming tool for solving problems related to their training and future profession.
Understanding and interpretation of texts and data, development of skills for their concretization and their clear and succinct exposition.
Aptitude for the distribution of resources and times and their implementation in real situations.
Ability to transmit concepts, ideas, processes, etc., related to Industrial Engineering orally and in writing, clearly and correctly.
Ability to use scientific-technical tools for solving calculation and design problems in Industrial Engineering and aptitude for searching for sustainable engineering solutions.
Ability for joint work and ability to develop multidisciplinary projects.
Ability to relate to other people and an open attitude towards creating new relationships.
Ability to incorporate new knowledge in the area of Industrial Engineering, based on the acquired training and necessary for the evolution of technology.
Development of autonomy and creativity capacities, which enhance aptitudes for developing own initiatives and undertaking new projects.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Encoding of integers and real numbers.
Encoding of sounds, images and videos on the computer.
Computer structure proposed by Von Neumann.
Real processors, dedicated and general purpose.
Types of memories: RAM and ROM.
Need for peripherals: utility and classification.
Types of languages: Assembly language vs. High-level language.
Concept of structured data: Static data structures, Dynamic data structures.
Flowcharts: Properties, symbols and basic rules of an algorithm.
Spreadsheet: How to work with the spreadsheet.
